subject: Human Evolution
title: Lactose Tolerance
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Lactose Tolerance.

hook.text: Most adult humans can't digest milk. If you can, you carry a mutation that's less than 10,000 years old.

buildup.text: All baby mammals produce lactase to digest milk. In most, the gene switches off after weaning.

discovery.text: Pastoralist populations evolved lactase persistence—the gene stays on into adulthood.

twist.text: It evolved independently in East Africa and Northern Europe—same solution, different mutations.

climax.text: Lactose tolerance is one of the strongest examples of recent natural selection in humans.

punchline.text: Milk drinking rewrote our genes in real time.

quiz.question: Why can some adults digest milk?
options: A recent mutation keeps the lactase gene active past childhood
Milk is easy to digest naturally
